post_read_steps: df = df.dropna(how='all')  # removes 2 trailing all-empty records (physical lines 14899-14900, literally ',,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,')
NOTE: do NOT strip the header -- the first column name is literally 'Sr. No. ' with a trailing space, and the file starts with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) which encoding='utf-8-sig' removes.
row_count_explanation: wc -l = 14900. The csv module yields 13703 logical records = 1 header + 13700 data rows + 2 trailing all-empty records. The 1197 extra physical lines are exactly the 1197 newline characters embedded inside quoted fields (322 rows carry a newline inside ADDRESS / Street/Locality / Formatted Address, e.g. Sr. No. 56 ADDRESS = 'Govt Hospital\nPunganur'). 13703 + 1197 = 14900. True logical row count is 13700.

columns.name: Sr. No.
columns.notes: 1..13700 with no gaps; the file's only unique column, but it is a positional ordinal, not a stable source identifier. Header literally contains a trailing space.

columns.name: STATE_NAME
columns.notes: 29 distinct. Non-LGD spellings: 'Tamilnadu' (LGD: Tamil Nadu), 'Pondicherry' (LGD: Puducherry), 'Jammu And Kashmir'. Goa, Nagaland, Delhi and all other UTs absent.

columns.name: DISTRICT_NAME
columns.notes: 663 distinct. Pre-rename / misspelled variants throughout (Jalor->Jalore, Sangali->Sangli, Gurgaon->Gurugram, Belgaum->Belagavi, G.B. Nagar->Gautam Buddha Nagar).

columns.name: BLOCK_NAME
columns.notes: 4443 distinct PMGSY block names. 879 rows have BLOCK_NAME == DISTRICT_NAME.

columns.name: HABITATION_NAME
columns.notes: 11607 distinct. PMGSY habitation, finer than a revenue village. 1465 rows (10.69%) have HABITATION_NAME == BLOCK_NAME (block-HQ habitations). 7 values carry a leading U+00A0.

columns.name: HAB_CODE
columns.notes: PMGSY/OMMAS habitation code, all numeric, 3-7 digits, range 349..1429221. NOT unique: 12092 distinct over 13700 rows; 1016 codes carry 2..48 rows. Never spans more than one state/district/habitation name, so it identifies the HABITATION, not the facility.

columns.name: MASTER_FACILITY_DESC
columns.notes: Free-text facility name entered by field staff. 8851 raw / 8172 normalised distinct. 4046 rows (29.53%) are nothing but a generic facility-type word (24-token generic list in scripts/05_deep.py; a wider variant list gives 4098 / 29.91%). 5723 rows (41.77%) have <=2 tokens.

columns.name: ADDRESS
columns.notes: Very thin: 60.90% are <=12 chars, 39.14% are byte-identical to HABITATION_NAME, only 224 rows contain a digit. 322 rows contain a literal newline.

columns.name: FILE_UPLOAD_DATE
columns.notes: %d-%b-%y. Parses 13637/13700; 63 nulls, all Tamil Nadu. Range 2019-01-09 .. 2022-11-26; 72.83% of rows (9978) are Aug-Dec 2019.

columns.name: MASTER_FACILITY_CATEGORY_NAME
columns.notes: Constant 'Medical' for all 13700 rows. In the wider PMGSY facility master this column also takes Education/Transport/etc values; this extract has already been filtered to Medical, so no schools/roads are present as a CATEGORY -- but see issues.md, a handful of non-health rows survive in the free-text name.

columns.name: SUB_CATEGORY
columns.notes: Only 2 values. This is PMGSY's own coarse label and it frequently disagrees with the facility name: 2546 of 6393 'Community Health Centre' rows have no CHC/community-health token in the name, and 89 of them are literally named 'hospital'.

columns.name: LATITUDE
columns.notes: Field-collected point, 8 decimal places on 81.3% of rows. 100% inside India's bbox, no zeros, no nulls.

columns.name: LONGITUDE
columns.notes: See LATITUDE.

columns.name: Postcode_py
columns.notes: Reverse-geocoder output (the _py suffix marks a Python geocoding pass). Byte-identical to 'Pincode' on 13700/13700 rows. Trustworthy only on the 11304 rows where address_py also echoes the same 6-digit token.

duplicates.method: near_dupe_name_geo = count of row pairs within 150 m (haversine via cKDTree on ECEF coords) whose lowercased alphanumeric-normalised MASTER_FACILITY_DESC has difflib SequenceMatcher ratio >= 0.85. Total pairs within 150 m = 1005; >=0.70 similarity = 285. Other definitions computed: duplicated (normname, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE) = 3; duplicated (LATITUDE, LONGITUDE) = 29; duplicated (normname, latlon rounded to 3dp ~111 m) = 54; duplicated (normname, HAB_CODE) = 21; duplicated (normname, DISTRICT_NAME) = 3066 (this last one is inflated by generic names such as 'CHC' and is NOT a dedup signal).

geo_quality.note: Best geo of any column in this file: 100% populated, 100% in-bbox, 0 zeros, 0 swaps, facility-level precision (48 distinct points inside a single HAB_CODE).

pincode_quality.note: Pincode is 100% populated but only 11304 rows (82.51%) are echoed by the geocoded address_py string; on those 11304 the two agree 100%. Of the 2396 uncorroborated rows, 443 carry a pincode whose first 2 digits do not appear on any corroborated row in the same state+district (control: 11304/11304 corroborated rows pass the same test). Treat the uncorroborated 17.49% as unreliable.

candidate_primary_key.note: 'Sr. No. ' is unique (1..13700, no gaps) but it is a spreadsheet row ordinal, not a source system key -- it will not survive a re-extract. HAB_CODE is NOT unique (12092 distinct / 13700 rows, max 48 rows per code) because it identifies a habitation, not a facility. Recommended surrogate: 'PMGSY:' || HAB_CODE || ':' || Sr. No.  , or the composite (HAB_CODE, MASTER_FACILITY_DESC, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE) which is unique across all 13700 rows.

grain.one_row_is: one health facility, located in one PMGSY habitation
evidence: HAB_CODE repeats: 1016 codes carry 2..48 rows, but within a repeated code the facility NAMES are all different and the lat/lon are all different (e.g. HAB_CODE 440318 = Jagatpur, Bareilly, UP has 48 rows: 'chanderlok hospital', 'medinova hospital', 'khushlok hospital', ... each with its own coordinate). That is many facilities in one habitation, not one facility linked to many habitations.

A habitation-facility link table would repeat the same facility under different habitations. It does not: only 1 (normalised-name, lat, lon) triple appears under more than one HAB_CODE, and only 7 exact (lat, lon) pairs do.
HAB_CODE never spans more than one STATE_NAME (0 codes), DISTRICT_NAME (0 codes) or HABITATION_NAME (0 codes), confirming it is a geographic key that is 1:1 with the habitation.
(HAB_CODE, MASTER_FACILITY_DESC, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE) is unique over all 13700 rows.

coded_vocabularies.HAB_CODE: 12092 distinct numeric PMGSY/OMMAS habitation codes, range 349..1429221 -- open vocabulary, needs the external OMMAS/LGD habitation master to decode. Not enumerated here.

er_readiness.note: Geo is the strong signal: 100% of rows carry a usable, facility-precision coordinate, so a geo-radius block (district + 250 m) works for every row. Name is the weak signal: 4046 rows (29.53%) have a name that is only a facility-type word ('CHC', 'bedded hospital', 'Dispensary') and cannot be matched on name at all. Address adds nothing (60.9% of ADDRESS values are <=12 chars and 39.1% just restate the habitation). Pincode is usable on the 82.5% of rows the geocoder corroborates. Recommended blocking key: state_raw + district_raw normalised to LGD + lat/lon rounded to 3dp, with name similarity as the scorer, NOT as the blocker.
